definitions.explanation: A fluid-filled bubble on the skin caused by friction, heat, or repeated pressure. Commonly occurs on the hands from gripping tools or on the feet from walking or ill-fitting shoes.
A thickened, hardened area of skin that develops from repeated friction or pressure over time.

examples.english: I got a blister on my hand.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{靴|くつ}を{履|は}いたら{足|あし}にマメができた。
examples.english: I got blisters on my feet from wearing new shoes.

examples.japanese: バットを{振|ふ}りすぎて、{手|て}のひらにマメがつぶれて{血|ち}が{出|で}た。
examples.english: I swung the bat so much that the blisters on my palms burst and bled.

examples.japanese: ギターを{弾|ひ}いていたら{指先|ゆびさき}にマメができた。
examples.english: I developed calluses on my fingertips from playing guitar.

examples.japanese: {鉄棒|てつぼう}の{練習|れんしゅう}で{手|て}にマメがたくさんある。
examples.english: I have lots of calluses on my hands from practicing on the horizontal bar.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{農作業|のうさぎょう}で{手|て}のマメがすっかり{硬|かた}くなった。
examples.english: After years of farm work, the calluses on my hands have become completely hard.

notes:
Usually written in katakana (マメ) or hiragana (まめ) to distinguish from {豆|まめ} (bean). The connection is that blisters and calluses resemble small beans in shape.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- マメができる: to get a blister/callus
- マメがつぶれる: a blister bursts
- マメが{硬|かた}くなる: a callus hardens
- {手|て}のマメ: blister/callus on the hand

USAGE:
The distinction between blister (fluid-filled) and callus (hardened skin) depends on context. Fresh マメ from short-term friction are blisters; long-term マメ from repeated activity become calluses.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {水膨|みずぶく}れ: water blister — specifically a fluid-filled blister
- たこ: callus; corn — hardened skin, often on feet
